name: Barcelona
tagline: Gaudí, Gothic lanes and a Mediterranean table
summary: Begin with a timed Sagrada Família visit, then group the Gaudí houses along Passeig de Gràcia. Save a separate walking half-day for the Gothic Quarter and El Born, with food stops and a hilltop or waterfront break.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn suit long walks; summer can be hot, busy and expensive. Timed attractions benefit from advance booking.
arrival: Barcelona–El Prat airport connects by rail, metro, bus and taxi. Choose the route closest to your accommodation and account for terminal transfers.
gettingAround: Use metro and buses between districts, then walk within each cluster. Park Güell and Montjuïc involve hills.
cashTip: Carry a modest amount of local cash for small purchases; use cards where accepted and check menu or ticket prices before paying.
foodTip: Try Catalan market cooking and tapas, then use specific vegetarian or operator-stated halal venues when needed.
buyTip: Look for ceramics, local design and packaged food; compare products away from the busiest tourist stalls.
baseArea: Eixample for transport and Gaudí; El Born or the Gothic Quarter for a walkable old-town base.

connections.note: Direct high-speed trains are possible; check date-specific departures and book ahead.

items.summary: A large covered market brings produce, spices, sweets and prepared food into one colourful walk.
items.expect: It is a useful place to compare small food purchases before choosing a meal elsewhere.
items.tip: Entry is free; spending is optional and tourist-facing stalls can be expensive. Respect vendors and shoppers.
